The community ana­lysis of soil bacteria in the four different treatments was performed using a paired–end method with MiSeq (Illumina), targeting the V3 and V4 regions of bacterial 16S genes.

The Quantitative Insights into Microbial Ecology (QIIME 2) pipeline ( Caporaso et al. , 2010 ) was used to remove low–quality and chimeric sequences. The sequences that passed preprocessing were obtained as amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) at 97% similarity, together with the representative sequences.

specification.input_notes: The BioProject PRJNA1112978 contains one run accession SRR29074840 (1,425,660 bytes). This is the raw sequencing data for the 16S amplicon analysis. No other data files are listed in the deposit. The paper does not provide sample metadata (treatment, time point) in the deposit listing; such metadata would be needed to reproduce the exact grouping.
specification.comparison_metric: The observed relative abundance of Streptomycetaceae in each treatment at one week post-incubation is compared to the reported percentages (2.0%, 3.2%, 7.7%, 18.9%).
specification.numerical_agreement_criterion: Proportions are compared by numerator/denominator: the reported percentages must match the computed relative abundance within the displayed rounding bin (one decimal place).
specification.specification_gaps: The paper does not specify: (1) the exact number of reads per sample or rarefaction depth; (2) the taxonomic classifier or database version used for assigning families (only EzBioCloud is mentioned for ASV identification); (3) whether relative abundances were calculated after rarefaction or as proportions of total reads; (4) the exact sample-to-run mapping (which run corresponds to which treatment/time point); (5) the handling of negative controls or contaminant sequences.
